title: Components of the generic proper/open transformation word
statement:
Let $A,C,D,E,T$ be categories, $I:A\to T$, $P:T\to C$, $Q:A\to D$, $L:D\to E$, $J:E\to D$, $H:D\to C$, $K:E\to C$, $R:A\to E$ functors, and let $b:I\mathbin{\gg}P\Rightarrow Q\mathbin{\gg}H$, $d:1_D\Rightarrow L\mathbin{\gg}J$, $t:J\mathbin{\gg}H\Rightarrow K$, $c:Q\mathbin{\gg}L\Rightarrow R$ be natural transformations; here $F\mathbin{\gg}G$ means first $F$, then $G$. Define $w:I\mathbin{\gg}P\Rightarrow R\mathbin{\gg}K$ by composing $b$, right whiskering of $Qd$ by $H$, right whiskering of the inverse associator of $Q,L,J$ by $H$, the associator of $Q\mathbin{\gg}L,J,H$, left whiskering of $t$ by $Q\mathbin{\gg}L$, and right whiskering of $c$ by $K$. For every object $M$ of $A$,
$$w_M=K(c_M)\circ t_{L(Q(M))}\circ H(d_{Q(M)})\circ b_M.$$
The constructor packages exactly this word before substituting concrete functors; it makes no new choice of any arrow.

source.place: whiskerLeft and whiskerRight, lines 44-65; associators in Functor/Category.lean lines 182-189; the same word is the definition of ordinary intrinsic alpha, Stacks Tag 0F7B refinement

proof.text: Evaluate the defining natural-transformation composite at M. The whiskering component formulas give b_M followed by H(d_QM), the image under H of the identity associator component, the second identity associator component, t_LQM, and K(c_M). Functors preserve identities, so these two identity factors disappear. Associativity gives the displayed four-factor formula. This argument includes empty categories and zero functors.

theorem properOpenCompositeTransformation_app
    (A C D E T : Type*) [Category A] [Category C] [Category D]
    [Category E] [Category T]
    (I : A ⥤ T) (P : T ⥤ C) (Q : A ⥤ D) (L : D ⥤ E)
    (J : E ⥤ D) (H : D ⥤ C) (K : E ⥤ C) (R : A ⥤ E)
    (b : I ⋙ P ⟶ Q ⋙ H) (d : 𝟭 D ⟶ L ⋙ J)
    (t : J ⋙ H ⟶ K) (c : Q ⋙ L ⟶ R) (M : A) :
    (properOpenCompositeTransformation A C D E T I P Q L J H K R b d t c).app M =
      b.app M ≫ H.map (d.app (Q.obj M)) ≫
        t.app (L.obj (Q.obj M)) ≫ K.map (c.app M)
